lines: Welcome to Module Five: Troubleshoot and Optimize.
It's about finding what's broken in a GPU server, fixing it cleanly, and making healthy servers fast.
It's three a.m., and an on-call engineer is paged again.
Training jobs keep dying, and every one of them ran on the same node.

say.0: It's three A M, and an on-call engineer is paged again.

lines: The tempting move is to guess: reboot the node, resubmit the job, and hope.
Hours later the job dies again, and nobody knows why.
So she starts with evidence: the kernel log shows Xid seventy-nine, a GPU that has fallen off the bus.
Running nvidia-smi confirms it, listing seven GPUs instead of eight.

say.0: So she starts with evidence: the kernel log shows zid seventy-nine, a GPU that has fallen off the bus.
say.1: Running en-vidia S M I confirms it, listing seven GPUs instead of eight.

lines: Next she checks the BMC event log, which records the server's own sensors.
A fan failed hours earlier, and the GPUs have been overheating and throttling ever since.

say.0: Next she checks the B M C event log, which records the server's own sensors.

lines: Now she follows the disciplined path: drain the node, so the scheduler stops sending it work.
Then collect a bug report, before touching any hardware.
The fan is swapped, and the damaged GPU goes back to the vendor under an RMA.
Only after diagnostics pass again does the node return to service.

say.0: The fan is swapped, and the damaged GPU goes back to the vendor under an R M A.

lines: A second node looks perfectly healthy, with no errors anywhere.
Yet every job on it runs noticeably slower than on its neighbours.
The culprit is the BIOS: it was left in a power-saving profile, with the wrong NUMA setting.
Fix both, and the node keeps pace with its peers.

lines: Lesson one teaches you to identify faulty GPUs, fans, NICs, and power supplies.
You'll read Xid errors, and use nvidia-smi, DCGM diagnostics, and NVSM health checks.

lines: You'll learn which Xid codes point to hardware, and which usually point to the application.
And the BMC event log catches what the operating system can't see, like failed fans and power supplies.

lines: Lesson two covers replacing faulty cards, GPUs, and power supplies.
The order matters: drain, collect logs, open an RMA, swap the part, re-validate, then resume.

lines: Lesson three optimises AMD and Intel servers, starting in the BIOS.
You'll set the power profile, choose the NUMA layout, and check PCIe and IOMMU settings.

And you'll tune storage, so data arrives fast enough to keep the GPUs busy.
